title: Introduction to Machine Learning
content: Machine learning is a field of artificial intelligence. Supervised learning trains predictive models on labeled data. Common algorithms include logistic regression, decision trees, and support vector machines.

title: Information Retrieval and Search Engines
content: A search engine retrieves relevant documents for keyword queries. Inverted indexing provides a mapping from each term to documents containing it. TF IDF weights and cosine similarity help rank documents efficiently.

title: Data Structures for Fast Search
content: Hash maps enable fast term lookups in an inverted index. Priority queues and heaps select the top K ranked results without sorting every candidate. Efficient query processing is essential at scale.

title: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
content: Convolutional neural networks learn visual features from images. Transfer learning can adapt pretrained image classification models to new datasets.

title: Natural Language Processing Fundamentals
content: Natural language processing analyzes text using tokenization, normalization, and text classification. Tokenization divides content into searchable terms; stop word filtering improves matching.

title: Cloud Deployment with Streamlit
content: Streamlit is a Python framework for building interactive web applications. Deploy Python apps through Streamlit Community Cloud after pushing code and dependency requirements to GitHub.

title: Understanding TF IDF
content: Term frequency measures how often a word appears within a document. Inverse document frequency discounts common terms across the collection. TF IDF supports ranking for information retrieval.

title: Android Malware Classification
content: Android application packages contain manifest metadata and classes dex bytecode. Static malware classification uses permissions, opcodes, and machine learning features to distinguish malicious and benign applications.

title: Python Algorithms Handbook
content: Python dictionaries implement hash table based lookups. The heapq package implements priority queue operations and efficient top K selection with nlargest.

title: Distributed Search Systems
content: Search engine scaling requires sharding document collections, caching queries, and parallel indexing. Distributed search services replicate shards and aggregate top ranked results across nodes.
